state.name: Virginia
state.peak_intrusion_season: March through May during spring raccoon and squirrel denning and groundhog emergence, the May 1 through August 15 bat maternity season under CNAP conditions, summer for skunk, groundhog, and copperhead activity, and late September through November as squirrels, rats, and bats seek winter shelter
state.climate_factor: Virginia runs from Atlantic and Chesapeake Bay Tidewater through the Piedmont to Blue Ridge and Allegheny karst country, so humid coastal summers, mild Piedmont winters that keep raccoons and opossums active, and cold mountain winters that push bats and rodents into structures all shape call volume in different parts of the state
state.permit_note: Virginia requires a Commercial Nuisance Animal Permit (CNAP), issued by the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources under 4 VAC 15-30-50, for commercial nuisance wildlife work; bat work requires additional DWR-recognized bat training from January 1, 2025, the CNAP does not authorize threatened or endangered species, federally protected migratory birds, black bear, white-tailed deer, or wild turkey, and Virginia prohibits trap-and-relocate — captured wildlife is released on the property's curtilage or humanely euthanized, with only snakes and, in no-firearm areas, squirrels eligible for the bounded off-site releases the permit conditions allow
